hook: A U.S. Air Force Special Operations aircraft returning from an ISR mission (Operation ENDURING SENTINEL) over the Gulf of Oman detected a glowing spherical object with a downward-projecting cylindrical pole flying straight over the water at 140 knots, formally reported as a UAP Incident to USCENTCOM and AARO.
why_it_matters: This report is notable for its unusually specific visual description: a 'glowing hot' spherical object with an 'unwavering cylindrical pole/bar' extending from its underside — an unconventional morphology not consistent with known aircraft or balloons. The document also reveals a discrepancy between the official metadata summary (which attributes 163 knots and 24,000 ft to the UAP) and the actual report text, where 163 knots and 23,999 ft are the *observer aircraft's* parameters, and 140 knots is the UAP's estimated velocity flying near sea level. Despite possessing an AN/DAS-1 targeting pod, the crew made no sensor interrogation attempt.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was described as a glowing, hot spherical object with a vertical cylindrical pole or bar attached to its underside, possibly producing a water reflection — a morphology inconsistent with standard aircraft or balloons.

quotes.text: GLOWING HOT SPHERICAL UNIDENTIFIED OBJECT WITH A VERTICAL UNWAVERING CYLINDRICAL POLE/BAR ATTACHED ON THE BOTTOM OF THE OBJECT POSS REFLECTION FROM THE OBJECT IN THE WATER, MOVING AT 140KNOTS

key_findings.finding: The UAP was observed flying straight and low over the water at 140 knots with unknown propulsion, while the observer aircraft was at 23,999 feet MSL traveling at 163 knots — indicating the UAP was operating at a drastically lower altitude than the reporting aircraft.

quotes.text: FLYING STRAIGHT JUST OVER THE WATER AT SPEED OF 140KNOTS

key_findings.finding: The crew made no sensor interrogation of the UAP despite being equipped with an AN/DAS-1 targeting pod (infrared/FLIR), and the observer assessed the UAP as benign with no advanced capabilities detected.

key_findings.finding: The UAP detection occurred during the return-to-base leg of a 10-hour ISR mission (Operation ENDURING SENTINEL) tasked with maritime surveillance of dhow traffic in the Gulf of Oman — the UAP sighting was incidental to the primary mission.

quotes.text: AT 0457Z, DURING RTB (b)(1)1.4a DETECTED 1X UAP (SEE UAP 1).
A. BEGIN SCANS AT 75NM WEST, NORTH, AND EAST OF SP FOR DHOWS TRANSITING IN THE DIRECTION OF SP

key_findings.finding: The report was filed by AFSOC's 3rd Special Operations Squadron (3 SOS), 27th Special Operations Wing, under USCENTCOM authority, and was formally approved for release to AARO — indicating the event entered the official UAP reporting chain.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' and uses AARO's standardized UAP Incident reporting fields throughout the MISREP form.
Intelligence dissemination throughout the document is classified 'SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY,' indicating Five Eyes partners were authorized recipients of the ISR tasking and reporting.
